## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates considerable internal reuse within the Pali tradition, identifying 138 matching passages across 49 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest match is found in the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, first part), with 26 shared segments amounting to 1,399 matching characters, including an alignment between §2.3–3.4 and commentary §1129–1131 [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Therāpadāna* itself, the text shares standard formulaic passages—particularly spanning verses §2.4–7.1—with other accounts of monastic past deeds involving floral offerings, notably the two *Punnāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* texts (Tha-Ap 161 and Tha-Ap 335), the *Minelapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 204), and the *Ekavandaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 232) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
